speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where on your leg the pain is located, and did you notice this limp suddenly or has it been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain in his knee occur specifically when he is active, and does it seem to ease up when he rests? Also, does he experience any stiffness in the hip or groin area in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain ever seem to radiate down into your thigh or groin area, or is it strictly confined to the knee? Also, when you walk, do you notice your left foot turning outward more than usual?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray

Since your knee pain might actually be coming from your hip, I need to see an image of your left hip to check for any issues like a slipped growth plate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray Left Hip: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease, which explains why your hip issues are causing pain in your knee. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
